How it was scored

  • Scanned with OpenSCAP in the image build on 2026-10-19 21:29 UTC.
  • Content: SCAP Security Guide 0.1.82, profile “CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark for Level 2 - Server” (xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_cis_level2_server), as published.
  • Score = rules passed ÷ (rules passed + rules failed). Every rule listed under Exemptions failed in the scan and counts as a failure in the score. Not-applicable and not-checked rules are not scored.
  • The build's OpenSCAP gate was enforced: floor 90%, and no failing rule without a documented exemption.

An OpenSCAP score measures this image against SSG content. It is not a certification, authorization or accreditation, and it is not an assessment of your system.

Exemptions (5)

Each rule below fails in the image for the reason given, and the last column is what you do to meet it on your instance. The reasons and actions come from the build record (this record is not covered by the bundle's signature).

RuleCategoryWhy it fails in the imageWhat you do
grub2_password
Set Boot Loader Password in grub2		AWS Marketplace policy: you complete it after launchAWS Marketplace policy prohibits meeting this rule in an AMI: "AMI must not contain hardcoded secrets such as system user and service passwords (including hashed passwords)" and "Password-based authentication for instance services is prohibited. This applies even if the password is generated, reset, or defined by the user at launch"; Linux AMIs "must allow users to get fully privileged access (for example, to allow sudo access)" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/product-and-ami-policies.html). The rule needs a boot loader or root password hash in the image, or a sudo password for the key-only default user.After launch run `sudo stigready-set-credentials` (installed in the image): it sets your own GRUB superuser and password, root password and a sudo password for your admin user, and removes NOPASSWD, which meets this rule on your instance.

Enable systemd-journal-upload Service		Remote log offload: needs your log serverThese rules send logs to the customer's central log server. The address, certificates and transport are the customer's; there is no log host we could point the image at.Point rsyslog (with TLS), auditd remote logging and/or systemd-journal-upload at your log server, with your CA.
